quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Rarely the committee approves a proposal without at least two rounds of revision."
quests.sentence: Rarely the committee approves a proposal without at least two rounds of revision.
quests.hint: When a negative adverb like 'rarely' opens the sentence, what happens to the order of the auxiliary and the subject?
quests.explanation: After a fronted negative adverb such as 'rarely', the auxiliary comes before the subject and the main verb returns to its base form: 'does the committee approve'.
quests.grammarRule: Inversion: Negative Adverbs at the Start of a Sentence

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Seldom did the manager had to remind the team about deadlines."
quests.sentence: Seldom did the manager had to remind the team about deadlines.
quests.incorrectPart: did the manager had to remind
quests.correctedPart: did the manager have to remind
options: did the manager had to remind
did the manager have to remind
the manager did have to remind
quests.correctAnswer: did the manager have to remind
quests.hint: Once 'did' carries the past tense in an inverted sentence, what form should the main verb take?
quests.explanation: After 'did', the main verb must return to its base form because 'did' already marks the past tense: 'did the manager have to remind'.
quests.grammarRule: Inversion: Auxiliary Carries the Tense

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Under no circumstances employees are permitted to share their login credentials."
quests.sentence: Under no circumstances employees are permitted to share their login credentials.
quests.incorrectPart: Under no circumstances employees are permitted
quests.correctedPart: Under no circumstances are employees permitted
options: Under no circumstances employees are permitted
Under no circumstances employees permitted are
Under no circumstances do employees are permitted
Under no circumstances are employees permitted
quests.correctAnswer: Under no circumstances are employees permitted
quests.hint: A negative phrase like 'under no circumstances' opens this rule. Which comes first afterward, the verb or the subject?
quests.explanation: A fronted negative phrase forces inversion, so the verb 'are' moves before the subject: 'Under no circumstances are employees permitted'.
quests.grammarRule: Inversion: Negative Phrases in Formal Rules

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Not only the software crashed, but it also deleted the entire project."
quests.sentence: Not only the software crashed, but it also deleted the entire project.
quests.correctedPart: Not only did the software crash
options: Not only did the software crash
Not only did the software crashed
quests.correctAnswer: Not only did the software crash
quests.hint: When 'not only' begins a sentence, what must come before the subject?
quests.explanation: 'Not only' at the start of a sentence triggers inversion with an auxiliary, so the sentence needs 'Not only did the software crash'.
quests.grammarRule: Inversion: Not Only at the Start of a Sentence

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "No sooner had the meeting started when the fire alarm went off."
quests.sentence: No sooner had the meeting started when the fire alarm went off.
quests.hint: 'No sooner' has a fixed partner word, and it is not the one used with 'hardly'. Which word completes the pair?
quests.explanation: 'No sooner' pairs with 'than', while 'hardly' pairs with 'when', so the sentence needs 'No sooner had the meeting started than'.
quests.grammarRule: Inversion: No Sooner ... Than

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Hardly the guests had arrived when the power went out."
quests.sentence: Hardly the guests had arrived when the power went out.
quests.hint: 'Hardly' at the start of a sentence works like other negative openers. Which comes first, the subject or 'had'?
quests.explanation: After a fronted 'hardly', the auxiliary moves before the subject, giving 'Hardly had the guests arrived when...'.
quests.grammarRule: Inversion: Hardly ... When

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Should you will need further assistance, please contact our support team."
quests.sentence: Should you will need further assistance, please contact our support team.
quests.hint: In a formal 'should' conditional, what form of the verb follows the subject?
quests.explanation: 'Should you need' replaces 'If you need', and the verb after the subject stays in the base form with no 'will'.
quests.grammarRule: Conditional Inversion: Should + Subject + Base Verb

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Were the company relocate, most employees would lose their jobs."
quests.sentence: Were the company relocate, most employees would lose their jobs.
quests.hint: In an inverted 'were' conditional about a hypothetical future event, which small word links the subject to the verb?
quests.explanation: The inverted form is 'Were' + subject + 'to' + base verb, so 'Were the company to relocate' means 'If the company relocated'.
quests.grammarRule: Conditional Inversion: Were + Subject + To + Base Verb

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Had disclosed the applicant her previous role, the panel would not have questioned her credentials."
quests.sentence: Had disclosed the applicant her previous role, the panel would not have questioned her credentials.
quests.hint: In an inverted past conditional, where does the subject go relative to 'had'?
quests.explanation: Inverted past conditionals put the subject directly after 'had', followed by the past participle: 'Had the applicant disclosed'.
quests.grammarRule: Conditional Inversion: Had + Subject + Past Participle

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "If she accepted the promotion last year, she would be managing the Berlin office now."
quests.sentence: If she accepted the promotion last year, she would be managing the Berlin office now.
quests.incorrectPart: If she accepted the promotion last year
quests.correctedPart: If she had accepted the promotion last year
options: If she accepted the promotion last year
If she had accepted the promotion last year
If she would accept the promotion last year
If she has accepted the promotion last year
quests.correctAnswer: If she had accepted the promotion last year
quests.hint: The if-clause refers to a specific past decision that did not happen, while the result is about now. Which tense marks the unreal past?
quests.explanation: A mixed conditional linking an unreal past to a present result uses the past perfect in the if-clause: 'had accepted'.
quests.grammarRule: Mixed Conditionals: Unreal Past, Present Result

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "If I am more organized, I would have finished the report before the deadline last week."
quests.sentence: If I am more organized, I would have finished the report before the deadline last week.
options: If I will be more organized
quests.hint: The if-clause describes a general quality that isn't true, while the result happened in the past. Which form marks the unreal present?
quests.explanation: An unreal present condition uses the past subjunctive 'were', so 'If I were more organized' pairs with the past result 'would have finished'.
quests.grammarRule: Mixed Conditionals: Unreal Present, Past Result

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "If the firm had not lost its main client, it would still employed two hundred people today."
quests.sentence: If the firm had not lost its main client, it would still employed two hundred people today.
quests.hint: The result is about the present day, so what verb form follows 'would'?
quests.explanation: Since the result concerns today, the main clause uses 'would' plus the base verb: 'would still employ'.
quests.grammarRule: Mixed Conditionals: Would + Base Verb for Present Result

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "It was the manager which announced the changes, not the director."
quests.sentence: It was the manager which announced the changes, not the director.
quests.incorrectPart: It was the manager which announced
quests.correctedPart: It was the manager who announced
options: It was the manager which announced
It was the manager whom announced
It was the manager who announced
It was the manager whose announced
quests.correctAnswer: It was the manager who announced
quests.hint: In a cleft sentence that emphasizes a person doing the action, which relative word follows?
quests.explanation: The emphasized noun is a person acting as the subject, so the cleft sentence uses 'who': 'It was the manager who announced'.
quests.grammarRule: Cleft Sentences: It + Be + Emphasized Noun + Who/That

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "What the client needs it is a clearer timeline, not more features."
quests.sentence: What the client needs it is a clearer timeline, not more features.
quests.incorrectPart: What the client needs it is
options: What the client needs it is
What the client needs that is
quests.hint: Does the 'what' clause need an extra pronoun before the verb 'is'?
quests.explanation: 'What the client needs' already works as the subject of the sentence, so adding 'it' repeats the subject unnecessarily.
quests.grammarRule: Emphasis Structures: What-Clauses as Subjects

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "It was not until the results were published then the team realized the error."
quests.sentence: It was not until the results were published then the team realized the error.
quests.hint: In an 'It was not until...' structure, which word introduces the main clause?
quests.explanation: The pattern is 'It was not until X that Y', so 'that' links the time phrase to the main clause.
quests.grammarRule: Cleft Sentences: It Was Not Until ... That

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The more you practice, more confident you become."
quests.sentence: The more you practice, more confident you become.
quests.hint: In a double comparative, both parts need the same marker. What is missing from the second part?
quests.explanation: The pattern is 'The more..., the more...', so the second part also needs 'the': 'the more confident you become'.
quests.grammarRule: Comparison: The More ... The More

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "This year's attendance was twice as higher as last year's."
quests.sentence: This year's attendance was twice as higher as last year's.
quests.hint: Multiplier comparisons like 'twice' work inside 'as ... as'. Should the adjective in the middle take an -er ending?
quests.explanation: 'As ... as' takes the base form of the adjective, so the sentence needs 'twice as high as', not 'as higher as'.
quests.grammarRule: Comparison: Multipliers with As ... As

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Our response times are as fast, if not faster than, those of our competitors."
quests.sentence: Our response times are as fast, if not faster than, those of our competitors.
quests.incorrectPart: as fast, if not faster than, those
quests.correctedPart: as fast as, if not faster than, those
options: as fast, if not faster than, those
as fast as, if not faster than, those
as fast, if not faster as, those
as fast than, if not faster than, those
quests.correctAnswer: as fast as, if not faster than, those
quests.hint: The first comparison is left unfinished by the interruption. Which word completes 'as fast'?
quests.explanation: Each comparison needs its own partner word: 'as fast as' and 'faster than'. Leaving out the first 'as' leaves the first comparison incomplete.
quests.grammarRule: Comparison: Completing Interrupted Comparisons

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The board insisted that the CEO resigns immediately."
quests.sentence: The board insisted that the CEO resigns immediately.
quests.hint: After verbs like 'insist' that express a demand, what verb form is used in the that-clause?
quests.explanation: Demand verbs take the base-form subjunctive in the that-clause, so the sentence needs 'resign', not 'resigns'.
quests.grammarRule: Subjunctive: Base Verb After Demand Verbs

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The judge ordered that the defendant does not contact the witness."
quests.sentence: The judge ordered that the defendant does not contact the witness.
quests.incorrectPart: that the defendant does not contact
options: that the defendant does not contact
that the defendant do not contact
that the defendant not to contact
quests.hint: In a subjunctive that-clause, how is a negative formed? Is 'do' or 'does' needed?
quests.explanation: The negative subjunctive places 'not' before the base verb without 'do': 'that the defendant not contact the witness'.
quests.grammarRule: Subjunctive: Negative Form After Order Verbs

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The regulations require that all drivers to carry proof of insurance."
quests.sentence: The regulations require that all drivers to carry proof of insurance.
quests.hint: After 'require that', does the verb need 'to', an -ing ending, or the plain base form?
quests.explanation: A that-clause after 'require' takes the base verb directly: 'that all drivers carry', with no 'to'.
quests.grammarRule: Subjunctive: Base Verb After Require That

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "By the time the new director arrives next month, we will complete the entire audit."
quests.sentence: By the time the new director arrives next month, we will complete the entire audit.
quests.hint: The audit will already be finished before another future moment. Which tense shows completion by then?
quests.explanation: 'By the time' plus a future point calls for the future perfect, which shows an action already complete: 'we will have completed'.
quests.grammarRule: Future Perfect: Completion Before a Future Point

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "She said she would call as soon as she will reach the hotel."
quests.sentence: She said she would call as soon as she will reach the hotel.
quests.incorrectPart: as soon as she will reach
options: as soon as she will reach
as soon as she has reached
as soon as she would reach
quests.hint: The sentence is set in the past after 'said'. Which tense fits the time clause after 'as soon as'?
quests.explanation: A time clause does not take 'will', and here the past frame set by 'said' and 'would call' calls for the simple past: 'as soon as she reached'.
quests.grammarRule: Tense Sequence: Time Clauses in a Past Frame

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The patient had been recovering well until the infection returns last week."
quests.sentence: The patient had been recovering well until the infection returns last week.
quests.incorrectPart: until the infection returns last week
quests.correctedPart: until the infection returned last week
options: until the infection returned last week
until the infection returns last week
until the infection had returned last week
until the infection has returned last week
quests.correctAnswer: until the infection returned last week
quests.hint: The phrase 'last week' points to a finished past event that interrupted the earlier recovery. Which tense fits?
quests.explanation: The interrupting event happened at a finished past time, so it takes the simple past: 'returned'. The earlier ongoing recovery stays in the past perfect continuous.
quests.grammarRule: Tense Sequence: Past Perfect Continuous with Simple Past

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The committee questioned to who the funds had been transferred."
quests.sentence: The committee questioned to who the funds had been transferred.
quests.hint: After a preposition in formal writing, which pronoun form is used for a person?
quests.explanation: A pronoun that follows a preposition takes the object form, so 'to whom' is correct, not 'to who'.
quests.grammarRule: Embedded Clauses: Whom After a Preposition

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The fact that the results were published early raise questions about the review process."
quests.sentence: The fact that the results were published early raise questions about the review process.
quests.hint: What is the true subject of the verb: 'the fact' or 'the results'?
quests.explanation: 'The fact that...' is a singular noun phrase, and the plural 'results' sits inside its clause, so the main verb is 'raises'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement: Subject with an Embedded That-Clause

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The auditor wanted to know how much would the repairs cost."
quests.sentence: The auditor wanted to know how much would the repairs cost.
quests.incorrectPart: how much would the repairs cost
quests.correctedPart: how much the repairs would cost
options: how much would the repairs cost
how much will the repairs cost
how much did the repairs cost
how much the repairs would cost
quests.correctAnswer: how much the repairs would cost
quests.hint: An embedded question inside 'wanted to know' uses statement order. Which comes first, the subject or 'would'?
quests.explanation: Embedded questions keep statement word order, so the subject comes before the modal: 'how much the repairs would cost'.
quests.grammarRule: Embedded Clauses: Statement Word Order in Noun Clauses

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "Only after the results had been verified the board agreed to publish the study."
quests.sentence: Only after the results had been verified the board agreed to publish the study.
quests.correctedPart: did the board agree to publish
options: did the board agree to publish
the board did agree to publish
quests.correctAnswer: did the board agree to publish
quests.hint: When 'only after...' opens the sentence, what happens to the word order in the main clause?
quests.explanation: A fronted 'only' phrase triggers inversion in the main clause, so the sentence needs 'did the board agree' with the base verb.
quests.grammarRule: Inversion: Only + Adverbial at the Start of a Sentence

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The chemicals, one of which are highly toxic, must be stored separately."
quests.sentence: The chemicals, one of which are highly toxic, must be stored separately.
quests.hint: In 'one of which', which word is the real subject of the verb?
quests.explanation: 'One' is the subject even though 'which' refers to the plural chemicals, so the verb is singular: 'one of which is'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement: One Of Which

quests.instruction: Select the correction that fixes the error in the sentence.
quests.question: Find and correct the grammatical error in this sentence: "The study found that participants who exercised regularly not only slept better but also reporting less stress than those who did not."
quests.sentence: The study found that participants who exercised regularly not only slept better but also reporting less stress than those who did not.
options: but also they reported less stress
but also to report less stress
quests.hint: Both parts of 'not only ... but also' need matching verb forms. What form follows 'slept'?
quests.explanation: Keeping both verbs in the simple past, 'slept' and 'reported', makes the 'not only ... but also' structure parallel.
quests.grammarRule: Parallelism: Not Only ... But Also
